summary: On this channel, views come mostly from the topic and the opening line, not from how long people keep watching. The strongest films stage a simple side-by-side test with cheap household objects and open with a short statement of the surprising result. General astronomy explainers, question hooks and history stories sit at the bottom. Caution: viewsPerDay favours younger films, and the newer animation-only, side-by-side films are also the youngest, so some of their lead may be age.

working.lesson: Side-by-side tabletop tests with everyday objects, where one of two identical setups behaves unexpectedly, are the top performers.
working.evidence: Paper bridge 436.3/day (2.2 days old), water bottle vortex 420.1 (3.0 days), raisin 369.6 (2.7 days) and toothpick 240.4 (2.0 days) average 366.6 views/day. Coanda spoon has the most total views of any film: 1,639 at 7.2 days.

working.lesson: Short statement hooks that state the visible result beat question hooks.
working.evidence: Among films of similar age (2.0–4.6 days), the six statement hooks average 306.9 views/day: paper 436.3, vortex 420.1, raisin 369.6, windshield 264.1, toothpick 240.4, tire 110.9. The three question hooks average 101.4: Mpemba 83.1, Moon 9…

working.lesson: A practical warning about something the viewer owns can travel well.
working.evidence: 'Hot water can crack your frozen windshield.' reached 264.1/day, 1,058 views and 18 likes, the most likes among films 2–4 days old. The other winter-car film, the tire light, only reached 110.9/day, so this is not guaranteed.

working.lesson: Space works when it is tied to a current, visible event or image (early sign, both films are young).
working.evidence: Starship catch: 556.3/day (1.8 days, 1,012 views). Jupiter's three shadows: 434.0/day (0.5 days). Evergreen astronomy explainers did far worse (see notWorking).

working.lesson: Fully animated films are doing at least as well as films with real photos, though age and writer are mixed in.
working.evidence: Animation-only films at least 2 days old average 320.6/day (5 films). Films with real photos average 126.5/day (17 films). The animation-only films are mostly the newer ones, so this is not a clean comparison.

working.lesson: Films of about 29–34 seconds sit at the top.
working.evidence: The six best films at least 2 days old run 29, 30, 31, 31, 34 and 34 seconds. Length alone does not separate them from the bottom group, which runs 25–37 seconds.

notWorking.evidence: Leonids 44.5/day, Moon illusion 92.9, Voyager 96.5, Hammer & feather 138.2, Seasons 145.3. Together they average 103.5 views/day.

notWorking.lesson: Question hooks ('Which…?', 'Why does…?', 'How can…?') trail statement hooks.
notWorking.evidence: Mpemba 83.1/day, Moon 92.9 and superheated microwave 128.2, against 306.9 for statement hooks of the same age.

notWorking.lesson: High retention does not by itself bring views here.
notWorking.evidence: Tightrope: 120.34% watched, 0.757 still watching at the end, relative 0.663, yet only 31.2/day (the lowest of films older than 2 days). Voyager: 115.56% watched, 96.5/day. Paper bridge: only 50.8% watched with relative 0.239, yet 436.3/day.

notWorking.lesson: Invention-history stories have not worked so far (one film only, an early sign).
notWorking.evidence: Microwave candy-bar origin, the only AI-media film: 81.6/day, 486 views at 6.0 days.

notWorking.lesson: Some films get almost no distribution, and the data does not show why.
notWorking.evidence: Copper pipe magnet: 4 views at 1.1 days (3.7/day). Cap vs Beak: 4 views at 0.5 days. Both were posted at 12:00, the only two films at that hour. Cap vs Beak also carried unrelated tags (#roblox, #bluetoothspeaker).

notWorking.lesson: Off-topic trend hashtags show no benefit.
notWorking.evidence: Egg spin (#eggrecipes, #food): 162.6/day. Ice slippery (#funny, #viralshorts): 145.9. Ice melts (#studywithme): 244.0 at 0.5 days, below the on-topic Jupiter (434.0) and zipper (369.9) films of the same age. Cap vs Beak (#roblox): 4 views.

rules: Open with one short statement (under 10 words) of the surprising visible result, not a question. Example: 'The swirled bottle empties first.'
Build the film around two identical household setups side by side, where one behaves unexpectedly.
Show both setups and the surprising outcome on screen within the first 3 seconds.
Keep the film between 29 and 34 seconds.
Pick kitchen or tabletop physics with objects everyone has (paper, bottles, cutlery, coins, water).
Only make space films when they are tied to a current event or a fresh image; skip evergreen astronomy explainers.
Use only hashtags that describe the film. No unrelated trend tags such as #roblox, #studywithme or #toys.
Put the objects and the surprise in the title, e.g. 'Paper Holds More Coins When Folded'.
moreTopics: Side-by-side kitchen experiments with household objects
Everyday objects behaving opposite to intuition (folded paper, swirled bottle, raisin in soda)
Practical warnings about things people own (windshield, car, appliances)
Space and tech tied to a current news event (Starship catch, a new Hubble or Jupiter image)
How small everyday mechanisms work (zipper slider), early sign at 369.9/day
lessTopics: Evergreen astronomy explainers (meteor showers, Moon illusion, seasons, Voyager distances)
Abstract physics concepts without a home demo (rotational inertia on a tightrope)
Myth-check topics framed as a question (Mpemba effect)
hooks: Paper holds more coins when you fold it.
This raisin rises while its twin stays put.
Hot water can crack your frozen windshield.
experiments: Post the next two films at 14:00 and 08:00 instead of 12:00. Both 12:00 films got about 4 views; 14:00 films average 245/day. Hour and film age are mixed in this data, so test it directly.
Make one evergreen space topic as an animated side-by-side test with a statement hook. This shows whether the topic or the format is what holds astronomy back.
Try a stronger final payoff in a top-format film to lift end retention (0.068–0.187 on the best films) and see whether views follow.
